meta.phase: Phase 0 — Positioning, Landscape Sweep & Competitive Deep Dive

evidence_grading.1: Primary — government publications, official statistics, official pricing pages, statutes, our own interviews/pilot data
evidence_grading.2: High-quality secondary — IIM/IIIT research, established consulting, World Bank/OECD, peer-reviewed
evidence_grading.3: Market intelligence — Tracxn, Crunchbase, Factly/Dataful, SaaS directories (G2, Capterra, GetApp)
evidence_grading.4: Community — vendor blogs, LinkedIn, Reddit, YouTube, review-site excerpts

reliability_markers.VERIFIED: read directly from a primary source
reliability_markers.NOT_PUBLIC: gated behind login or sales call
reliability_markers.UNVERIFIED: could not be confirmed; do not cite externally

records.claim: 64,756 HEIs on AISHE frame; 1,289 universities, 48,246 colleges, 15,221 standalone (2023-24)
records.notes: Latest published AISHE edition. 2024-25 still in error-rectification.

records.claim: AISHE 2023-24 university breakdown: State Private 464, State Public 462, INI 159, Deemed-Private 82, Central 55, Deemed-Govt 33, State Open 17
records.notes: Report contains an internal conflict on response counts (1278/46468/11787 vs 1249/44380/10513). Cite the named table.

records.claim: UGC lists 1,153 universities (57 Central, 482 State Public, 478 State Private, 136 Deemed) as of 31.03.2024
records.notes: Different frame from AISHE. Do not mix the two counts. See OQ-06.

records.claim: 8,489 AICTE-regulated technical institutions; 823 medical colleges; 17,752 teacher training institutions
records.notes: PRS compiling regulator data, not a direct AICTE publication.

records.claim: Autonomous colleges: 578/579 on AISHE dashboard
records.notes: Dashboard vintage unlabelled and exceeds published AISHE 2023-24 totals. See OQ-07.

records.claim: More than 6,400 IICs established in HEIs; 63,288 I&E activities by IICs in AY 2021-22
records.notes: LAST OFFICIAL PIB IIC COUNT — four years stale. Current figure UNVERIFIED. See OQ-01.

records.claim: KAPILA 2,746 institutes registered; 11,768 patents reimbursed; HEI patent filings 15,383 (FY23) to 33,675 (FY25), +119%
records.notes: Strongest quantified IPR demand signal found. Several other infographic values not machine-extractable.

records.claim: 83 AIC + 20 ACIC = 103 centres across 28 States/UTs; 6,782 startups incubated; 48 pending establishment
records.notes: Use 83. AIM website says 72, AIM AIC page says 69 (stale Jan 2024). See OQ-05.

records.claim: 10,000+ Atal Tinkering Labs across 733 districts; 1.1 crore+ students; 16 lakh+ innovation projects; AIM outlay Rs 2,750 cr to Mar 2028
DST/NSTEDB: 12,000+ startups supported; 175+ TBIs backed; 1,100+ IP; 1,30,000+ jobs
records.notes: DST page says 'more than 160 TBIs' — conflicts with 175+. Name the source whenever citing.

records.claim: BIRAC BioNEST: 74 bio-incubators; 1,102,430 sq ft; 3,157 incubatees; 800+ products commercialised; 1,300+ IPs filed
records.notes: Same page's table footer reads 'Showing 1 to 10 of 75' — internal 74/75 conflict.

records.claim: MeitY Startup Hub: 6,148+ startups, 517+ incubators, 329+ labs
records.notes: Closest official national incubator count. Per-state counts NOT published anywhere. See OQ-08.

records.claim: 2.23 lakh+ DPIIT-recognised startups; 23.36 lakh+ direct jobs; 1.07 lakh (48%) women-led; 55,200+ recognised in FY 2025-26
records.notes: 55,200+ in FY2025-26 is the highest ever in a year.

records.claim: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme: Rs 945 cr corpus; 219 incubators selected; 3,400+ startups funded; Rs 605 cr approved
records.notes: Jan 2026 said 215+ incubators — growth, not conflict.

records.claim: 31 of 36 States/UTs have a dedicated Startup Policy; 27 developed after Startup India (2016); startups in 653 districts
records.notes: The list of 31 states is login-gated and could not be extracted. See OQ-14.

records.claim: Fund of Funds for Startups: Rs 10,000 cr corpus; Rs 7,000+ cr to 135+ AIFs; Rs 26,900+ cr into 1,420+ startups; FFS 2.0 notified
Startup definition revised by G.S.R. 108(E): turnover ceiling Rs 100 cr to Rs 200 cr; 20 years recognition for Deep Tech; cooperatives eligible
records.notes: CRITICAL for data model: historic records use the old definition; recognition numbers now bifurcate standard vs Deep Tech.

records.claim: IIC portal dashboard: MIC programme participation, IIC performance, activity status, council status, student/faculty participation, incubation unit registration, e-Repository
records.notes: Primary evidence that the mandated portal is a compliance ledger, not an operating system.

records.claim: If council meeting not uploaded for a quarter, 'Add to My Calendar' is unavailable — no activities can be added. Minimum 2 council meetings/yr
records.notes: Hard sequential dependency: a governance artefact gates the reporting form.

records.claim: IIC activity minimums: 3 IIC Calendar activities/quarter (12/yr) + 1 Celebration/quarter (4/yr); baseline 16+ activities/yr
records.notes: 'Conducting the event alone will not secure the stars — the activity should be approved by the IIC.'

records.claim: Per-activity report requires 4 social media links, 3-way participant counts, expenditure, video URL, 2 photographs and a document upload
records.notes: The manual-work burden, field by field.

records.claim: IIC has a menu item 'IPR/TTO Centres' — registers a TTO's existence and floor area, but has no field to record a patent
records.notes: Sharpest single proof of the category error. Institutions register their IP office but cannot record their IP.

records.claim: YUKTI-NIR categories: Idea/PoC (TRL 1-4), Innovation/Prototype (TRL 5-9), Business/Startup; HEI-side verifier workflow; status Recommended/Not Recommended
records.notes: TRL banding is a government requirement that no commercial competitor implements.

records.claim: Data entered in YUKTI-NIR acts as input for ARIIA; verified innovations auto-pool into ARIIA Section 4 ranking data
records.notes: Single highest-value integration target identified in Phase 0. Selling into an existing budget line.

records.claim: 'IIC login credentials and the YUKTI login credentials are different'
records.notes: Evidence of credential fragmentation across mandated systems.

records.claim: NIRF Innovation 2025 parameters: FSI 0.25, IA 0.15, RIO 0.30, PII 0.10, AIE 0.10, Perception 0.10
records.notes: FSI fell 0.30 to 0.25; AIE rose 0.05 to 0.10. NIRF 2026 weights UNVERIFIED.

records.claim: NIRF FSI startup sub-metric: SU = 20 x f(N_vsp), where N_vsp = DPIIT/Startup India recognised startups in the previous three years
records.notes: 5 marks of the final Innovation score hinge on a single countable.

records.claim: NIRF Innovation data capture requires per-startup: name, DPIIT no, amount, funding org, year, achievement level, investment type — repeated per discipline per year
records.notes: None of these auto-populate from MCA, GST, ROC or DPIIT.

records.claim: NIRF does not gate submission — institutions publish their own submitted DCS PDFs publicly (verified live at NIT Rourkela, IIM Goa, JBIET, Rajah Serfoji)
records.notes: De facto open export of institution-submitted innovation data. Feeds GOV-030.

records.claim: NIRF institution-wise DPIIT startup dataset: 6,817 rows, 204 institute_ids, 5,490 distinct ventures, 4,538 registration numbers, 26 states, 80 cities, years 2024-2026
records.notes: Paywalled. Universe is only 202 institutions — the innovation-active elite, not the HEI population. 0.98% dirty-record rate. Proof of concept for StartupHub's own data asset.

records.claim: ARIIA DCS fetches institution performance from IIC, NISP, YUKTI and Innovation Ambassador portals, 'has reduced data submission efforts at the institute level by checking redundancy'
records.notes: Strongest official acknowledgement that duplication is a known problem. Limit: one-directional fetch, ARIIA-scoped only, does not remove NIRF-I.

records.claim: AISHE is not a significant innovation-data collector — innovation-adjacent items are binary (NIRF participation yes/no, NAAC, NBA, MoU counts)
records.notes: Corrects a common assumption. Heavy innovation burden lives in NIRF-I and ARIIA, not AISHE.

records.claim: 'Participation in AISHE is voluntary, and the data is self-reported by the HEIs... the quality of data is generally taken care of by the respective HEIs'
records.notes: Official acknowledgement of self-reporting quality risk.

records.claim: Standalone institutions responded at only 77.4% (11,787 of 15,221) in AISHE 2023-24 — the weakest category
records.notes: Participation evidence for unmeasured segments.

records.claim: SRF 5.0 results announced 16 Jan 2026; 34 States/UTs; 19 Action Points; 6 Reform Areas; Best Performer Cat A = Gujarat
records.notes: Per-State report PDFs published. Reports surface institutional support metrics.

records.claim: Maharashtra Startup Policy 2025 commits to an online system mapping all startups, incubators, accelerators, innovation hubs/labs, investors and mentors under a unique ID
records.notes: Most forward-looking state commitment in India. Simultaneously StartupHub's largest future partner and largest future threat.

records.claim: NIDHI-PRAYAS 2.0: students/faculty must submit a No Objection Certificate confirming IP vests entirely with the innovator or startup
records.notes: Hard institutional IP-vesting requirement. No platform tracks NOC issuance.

records.claim: MeitY Investment Playbook mandates TRL benchmarking and IP due diligence: ownership clarity, freedom to operate, defensibility; distinguishes ownership vs limited-term (2-year) university tech-transfer licence
records.notes: Defines the diligence standard TRL+IP features must satisfy to be credible.

records.claim: BHASKAR (Bharat Startup Knowledge Access Registry) launched 16 Sep 2024 by DPIIT; issues BHASKAR ID as ecosystem-universal identity
records.notes: Registration runs in parallel with, not instead of, DPIIT recognition.

records.claim: DPIIT plans to overhaul BHASKAR into a 'National Startup Master Data' registry tracking the startup lifecycle; MeitY Startup Hub floated a similar tender
records.notes: UNVERIFIED — trade-press report of a plan, not a notification. MOST IMPORTANT WATCH ITEM. See OQ-11.

records.claim: MAARG is the national mentorship platform with AI matchmaking, session scheduling, cohort programmes and dashboards
records.notes: Most operationally capable system in the mandated stack — but scoped to recognised startups, not institutional portfolios.

records.claim: Kerala Startup Mission operates 375+ IEDCs across colleges and universities, 27 R&D institutions, 63 incubators; issues a KSUM UID as a third identity layer
records.notes: Most developed institution-facing state innovation programme in India.

records.claim: No public API, developer documentation or bulk export found for IIC, YUKTI, NIRF, AISHE or MAARG
records.notes: NEGATIVE FINDING, deliberately logged. Removes a build-vs-buy option and makes migration a paid service opportunity.

records.claim: IIC's official 'Rating and Scoring System' help page returns 'Coming Soon' — star-rating formula is not publicly documented
records.notes: BLOCKS a feature. See OQ-10.

records.claim: NestLens Orbit: Launch Rs 75,000/yr; Starter Rs 99,000; Growth Rs 1,25,000; Scale Rs 2,50,000/yr; Enterprise custom
records.notes: MOST IMPORTANT PRICE ANCHOR. Vendor also publishes a conflicting Orbit PM/OS price list on the same domain.

records.claim: NestLens Orbit covers NIDHI, DST-TBI, BIRAC, RKVY-RAFTAR grant ledgers, compliance calendar, and Sarvam-powered Indian-language MOM transcription
records.notes: Closest existing competitor. Indian-language AI transcription is the one genuinely novel India-specific AI feature found anywhere.

records.claim: EcoSync: 'We do not hold SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification... We do not publish an uptime SLA... our first incubator is still our reference customer rather than our hundredth.' One customer: TBI-KIET
records.notes: Self-declared weakness. Procurement-aware buyers can disqualify on this today. Only competitor with GST/TDS/UPI/Razorpay depth.

records.claim: Incubatee (SCIP): Rs 25,000/month + Rs 75,000 one-time + Rs 10,000 mobile app + Rs 850/admin/month = Rs 3,95,200 year one
records.notes: Highest verified Indian price point, 3-5x Orbit. Page body says 'Pay as you use' contradicting the fixed table.

records.claim: IncubatX: Foundation Rs 10,000-15,000/mo; Accelerator Rs 30,000-40,000/mo; Executive AI Rs 50,000-60,000/mo; Media Kit Rs 15,000/mo
records.notes: Cheapest credible INR entry. Only vendor publishing a named government-scheme directory. Founded 2026, zero verifiable customers, 'SOC 2-ready' not certified.

records.claim: Accubate: Capterra 4.8 from 26 reviews — most-reviewed vendor in category. Customers incl. NSRCEL, NASSCOM, TCS, Hero MotoCorp, NCL, KPMG, Accenture
records.notes: Only real reference base in the category. Only verified Indian user complaint: 'No User manual!!' (Incubation Lead, 4 Sept 2024).

records.claim: AcceleratorApp: core platform from $499/mo (~Rs 5.4L/yr). Funding module published at $549-899/mo. ISO/IEC 27001 certified. Customers incl. Yale, MIT Design X, Max Planck, CGIAR. Zero Indian institutions.
records.notes: Inside StartupHub's band at the top. Best academic logo list in the market but no India presence, no INR, no Indian schemes, no IPR module.

records.claim: Founderhood: Free (15 startups/program); Starter $199/mo; Premium $649/mo; Advanced custom. Universities eligible for a 15% discount
records.notes: Best free tier in category. Only vendor actively courting university buyers on price. Starter at ~$169/mo (~Rs 1.4L/yr) is the credible global price objection.

records.claim: Gohorto: pricing page is a JavaScript application returning no figures. GetApp lists 'from $399/month'. Claims 'G2 High Performer 2026'. Only 3 GetApp reviews exist, one vendor-referred.
records.notes: Credibility concerns: badge claims rest on 3 reviews; self-authored comparison pages rate themselves 4.8 and rivals 2.1-3.6.

records.claim: incuTrack: Starter $75/mo, Premier $250/mo quarterly; $595 one-time setup incl. 6-month training. Mentor Matching $30/mo + $90 setup. G2 3.8 from 10 reviews.
records.notes: Category's most mature product (copyright Cybergroup Inc. 2002) and only one doing key control, work orders, insurance tracking. Recent G2 reviews call it 'quite outdated'.

records.claim: VentureLink: Lite free forever; Core $180/mo or $1,730/yr + $500 setup; no per-user fees. Add-ons: emails $25-60/mo, jobs $15, courses $20-50, events $30
records.notes: 'No per-user fees' is a genuine structural advantage for institutions with large founder/mentor populations. But 2 employees, zero customers, zero reviews.

records.claim: RiserNest: EUR 399/799/1500 per month (per team) OR EUR 40/70/120 per user/month. Full white-label with own domain AND own mobile apps. Case study: Frank and the Backs, 428 founders, 220+ startups, 62 mentors.
records.notes: Strongest white-label in category. Best-documented real-scale deployment. Two contradictory pricing models on one page.

records.claim: Innoloft/LoftOS: Free (5 users) to $29/$349/$849/mo. No-code portal builder WITH an accelerator program template — a university IT team could build its own for $29-349/mo
records.notes: THE DIY THREAT. Free templates for Accelerator, Incubator, Fellowship, Tech Transfer, Corporate Venture, Grant Program. Case study: RWTH Aachen University (Collaeb).

records.claim: Elsevier Pure public UK G-Cloud 14 price list: Core Module GBP 19,406/yr (Tier 1) to GBP 58,504/yr (Tier 5); Setup GBP 13,500 one-off; each integration GBP 5,188
records.notes: Hardest pricing benchmark available. Minimum Indian university deployment ~GBP 33,016/yr (~Rs 44.6L/yr) plus GBP 32,250 onboarding (~Rs 43.5L). Pure does not manage startups, cohorts, mentors or incubation.

records.claim: IdeaScale: Engage USD 12,999 / Evolve USD 21,999 / Advance USD 34,999 / Transform USD 64,999 — all TWO-YEAR subscriptions, no free plan
records.notes: ~$6,500/yr entry tier = ~Rs 5.85L/yr. Corporate intrapreneurial; assumes employee base, SSO, IT dept. Not a university/incubator fit.

records.claim: Applied (applied.co) is Applied Intuition, an autonomous-vehicle company — there is no accelerator management platform at applied.co. Bezu, Value Design Lab, Envisage, IdeaForge, Gobi: no evidence these exist as incubator software.
records.notes: Removes four phantom competitors from the original watchlist. Do not cite.

records.claim: Notion Plus $10/member/mo; audit log Enterprise-only. Notion 'does not enforce referential integrity'; relations export to CSV as plain URLs and cannot be re-imported.
records.notes: Most dangerous pricing neighbourhood: 8 editors on Notion Plus ~$960/yr (~Rs 86k), inside StartupHub's band. No audit log, no offline, no Indian compliance.

records.claim: Airtable Team $20/editor/mo; automation runs capped at 100 (Free) / 25,000 (Team) / 100,000 (Business). Airtable publishes contradictory limits: Business records 100,000 on pricing card vs 125,000 in help centre.
records.notes: 8 editors ~$1,920/yr (~Rs 1.73L/yr). Quota walls hit before scale does.

records.claim: Superhuman Docs (ex-Coda, acquired by Grammarly Dec 2024, renamed Oct 2025, product rebrand completed 8 Jul 2026): Pro $12/Doc Maker/mo. Audit events, SCIM, SAML, SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA all Enterprise-only.
records.notes: A direct competitor renamed twice in 20 months with roadmap attention split across three sibling products.

records.claim: Trello Standard $5/user/mo; Asana Starter $10.99; Monday Basic $9/seat; ClickUp Unlimited $7. At 10 users: Trello ~Rs 54k, ClickUp ~Rs 76k, Monday ~Rs 97k, Asana ~Rs 1.19L per year
records.notes: Anchors the floor of the price band. No domain model, no intake workflow, no IPR, audit logs Enterprise-only.

records.claim: No Indian campus ERP vendor found with a genuine startup-incubation module. AskERP is closest (grant management, patents tracker) but has no startup portfolio, IIC workflow, mentorship or incubation.
records.notes: They compete for the compliance budget (NAAC/NBA/NIRF/AISHE), not the innovation budget — but they own the relationship, data and procurement precedent.

records.claim: Google Workspace Business Starter India ~Rs 1,918-3,240 per user/year (~Rs 160-270/month)
records.notes: Google Sheets arrives bundled in licences the institution already pays for — zero marginal procurement cost.

records.claim: WhatsApp Business Platform India from 1 Oct 2026: Marketing Rs 0.8631/delivered message; Utility/Authentication/Service Rs 0.115 after first 1,000 free replies/month
records.notes: Removes free business-initiated nudges — weakens the free WhatsApp incumbent for institutions using it for mentor reminders.

records.claim: 'IISc Students - Join this Whatsapp group for updates' — IISc's IIC routes student coordination through WhatsApp
records.notes: India's most research-intensive institution. Strongest single piece of evidence that WhatsApp is the operational database.

records.claim: The IIC charter formally requires institutions to 'Create an Institution's Innovation portal to highlight innovative projects'
records.notes: Explains the ubiquity of hand-built static IIC sites (VIT, IISc, MGIT, PSG Tech, OPJU, ITM) — and explains why they rot.

records.claim: MasterSoft lists 'Multiple Excel Sheets for Data Entry Resulting in Human Errors'; DigiERP states 'departments still outside the system keep their own registers... you carry both the software cost and the duplicate work'
records.notes: Indian ERP vendors themselves market against spreadsheet duplication. Tier 4 — vendor marketing, not research.

records.claim: IIT Madras: 112 startups incubated FY25-26, 567 total portfolio, 431 patents filed in FY25-26; IP Management Cell under ICSR handles early-stage disclosures, prior-art evaluation, prosecution and portfolio management; plus a TTO
records.notes: The scale benchmark for what a mature institutional innovation operation actually requires software to handle.

records.claim: 'a typical firm has to navigate around 1,500 Acts which collectively impose 69,233 separate compliances and 6,618 independent filings'
records.notes: Institutions are compliance-saturated. A tool that reads as 'more compliance' is dead on arrival; a tool that reduces re-keying has a strong pitch.

records.claim: Standalone institutions responded at only 77.4% in AISHE 2023-24; AISHE 2024-25 had to be reopened for data error rectification until 24 Dec 2025
records.notes: Mechanism churn and low response are themselves evidence of data-entry friction.

records.claim: 'We ran the incubator on bunch of disconnected tools, multiple spreadsheets, and a lot of emails. VentureLink replaced all of it... how much time came back to the team!' — Ignacio Mongrell, Assistant Director, ICUBE, University of Toronto
records.notes: Named university customer quote, but vendor-published and unverifiable. Use as sentiment, not evidence.

records.claim: Notion's own help docs: audit log records events 'starting from the time of upgrade' — no retroactive history. Enterprise pricing is 'Contact Sales'.
records.notes: The decisive gap versus StartupHub: institutions need retroactive audit trails for accreditation and grant audits.

records.claim: ARIIA data collection requires 'Patent Application No', 'Year of Patent Application', 'Current Status', 'IP / Patented Technology' per innovation
records.notes: Direct proof that patent-level fields are mandated but no mandated system captures them.
